artists.biography:
Spiritualized are a British space rock band formed in 1990 in Rugby, Warwickshire by Jason Pierce (who often goes by the alias J. Spaceman) after the demise of his previous band Spacemen 3. The membership of Spiritualized has changed from album to album, with Pierce — who writes, composes and sings all of the band's material — being the only constant member.

Spiritualized have released seven studio albums. The best known and most critically acclaimed of these is perhaps 1997's Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space, which NME magazine named as their Album of the Year.

perplexity.description:
Songs in A&E is the sixth studio album by English rock band Spiritualized, released in May 2008 on Sanctuary Records in the UK and Fontana Records in the US. The album marked the band's return after a five-year hiatus following 2003's Amazing Grace, during which frontman Jason Pierce experienced a severe health crisis in 2005 involving advanced periorbital cellulitis and bilateral pneumonia that required intensive care hospitalization. The album's title and thematic foundation derive directly from Pierce's extended stay in the Accident and Emergency ward during his recovery, and the work is dedicated to the staff at the Royal London Hospital.

Musically, Songs in A&E continues Spiritualized's exploration of space rock and experimental rock aesthetics, blending orchestral arrangements with the band's characteristic neo-psychedelic approach. The 18-track album features the lead single "Soul on Fire," released in May 2008, alongside cover material including a rendition of Daniel Johnston's "True Love Will Find You in the End." Pierce described the album as "the work of The Devil...with a little guidance from me," suggesting a darker, more introspective sonic palette shaped by his personal ordeal.

The album received recognition within the critical community, with the American webzine Somewhere Cold ranking it No. 6 on their 2008 Hall of Fame awards. Songs in A&E was released across multiple formats including standard CD, limited edition book editions, and double 12" vinyl in the UK, reflecting the band's commitment to physical media presentation.
